### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**24** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `27f5678d633218f3377eafcd217693fb09e9cbda` — the merge of head `3ff6dc9817c619ed2c18282bb9979a4c00eb226f` into base `385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 27f5678d633218f3377eafcd217693fb09e9cbda && git checkout 27f5678d633218f3377eafcd217693fb09e9cbda
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca 3ff6dc9817c619ed2c18282bb9979a4c00eb226f && git checkout -B drift-repro 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca && git merge --no-ff 3ff6dc9817c619ed2c18282bb9979a4c00eb226f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5664ba5f014ce57373806f0a294a612907aa8bf5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.lookup-filter-record-reference-shape-refused.ts + packages/spec/src/data/field.test.ts, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json, packages/spec/api-surface/data.json, packages/spec/export-origins/data.json, packages/spec/declaration-map/data.json, packages/spec/json-schema.manifest/data.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json, packages/spec/liveness/field.json

Inputs read: card #34009 body and all six comments (triage 6897901853, claims 6898152905 / 6898169994, os-dev-report 6900208284, seat rulings 6900252552); PR #34078 body and file list; the net diff `529ed7d9..5664ba5f` (16 files, +445/-24); the 68 check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx`, `RecordPickerDialog.tsx#lookupFiltersToRecord`, `packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts`, `packages/spec/src/shared/refinement-projection.ts`, the `dependsOn` describe in `field.zod.ts`. `.changeset/**` and `content/docs/**` are prose faces (lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`); the changeset was read for ② only.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set widened, `lookupFilters[]` gains `orEmpty?: boolean`** — right. Optional, strict-object key; six near-miss spellings alias to it.
- **Accept set narrowed, a `value` object owning a `$record` key outside the declared shape is refused** (path not `seg` or `seg.seg` in the field-key grammar, any key beside `$record`, operator `in` / `notIn` / `contains`) — right as a narrowing. The path regex equals `FIELD_KEY_GRAMMAR` (`object.zod.ts`) per segment, so no legal field name is refused. Every refused shape was already refused at query time: the picker lowers `eq` to `{ field: value }` and the rest to `{ field: { $op: value } }`, the door refuses an object comparand under an operator (pinned by the new test), and the `eq` shorthand reaches the driver, whose default arm throws the unsupported-operator refusal (`sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts`, read at the head). Nothing that worked is taken away.
- **Accept set narrowed, `orEmpty` under `in` / `notIn` / `contains` refused** — right; a new key, so no stored document is affected.
- **Unchanged and confirmed by the control test**: literals, lists, `{today}`, `{current_user_id}`, `{ $now, addDays }`, `{ $field }` still parse. A `{ $record }` object as a MEMBER of an `in` list is not judged (see N3).
- **Public surface, three new exports from `@objectstack/spec/data`** (`LookupFilterRecordReferenceSchema`, `LookupFilterRecordReference` = `z.input`, `LookupFilterRecordReferenceParsed` = `z.infer`) — right; api-surface and export-origins carry all three, declaration-map and json-schema.manifest carry the schema, authorable-surface carries `data/LookupFilterRecordReference:$record`. Ruled by the seat (ruling 4).
- **`dropped-refinements.baseline.json` grows by 12 sites (1069 to 1081; +13/-1 lines)** — the growth is right. The new rule is a cross-key conditional (operator enum against `value` shape / `orEmpty`), and the closed projection list (`refinement-projection.ts`: required-one-of, non-blank-string, dependent-required, banned-keys, banned-key-pattern, unique-items) has no arm for it, so it cannot leave the ledger in this PR. One site on `data/Field` plus eleven embedding schemas, each `…lookupFilters.element`; 12 added lines counted, the measured total moves by 12. The ledger's shrink-only rule is about repairs; a new unprojectable rule is recorded, not hidden. Adding an arm would be its own public-contract decision.
- **`liveness/field.json` `lookupFilters` note** — the added sentences agree with the reader: `lookupFiltersToRecord` passes `value` through and has no `orEmpty` read. Status stays `live` for the key, with the two new members dated as declared ahead of the reader. Right.
- **Check-runs on the head**: 56 success, 10 skipped, 2 failure. The failures are `Test Core (7/8)` (job 132919232970) and its aggregate `Test Core`. Read from the full job log: the one failing task is `@objectstack/scenarios#test`, `packages/qa/scenarios/test/runner/run-date.test.ts`, two cases (`run on 2028-02-28`, `run on 2028-03-31`), both `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms`; 881 of 883 pass, 73 of 74 turbo tasks succeed. The package is not in this diff, the scenarios leg's log holds no `lookupFilters` or `$record` line, and the signature is the one issue #34081 anchors (`Queue-flake anchor: test/runner/run-date.test.ts`, open, 11 PRs ejected). Not attributed to this PR. It is still red on this head and needs a re-run before landing. Every spec gate (liveness, generated artifacts, changeset, PR-body guards, type checks, Test Core 1-6 and 8) is green.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`. The diff publishes only `@objectstack/spec`. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is in the closed set (`added|narrowed|semantic|none`) and is the right member: a value refused outranks the key added. A kind takes at least `minor` — matches.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on both the PR body and the changeset, with the BREAKING banner, the FROM/TO remedy and `adr-0087: registered lookup-filter-record-reference-shape-refused`. Matches the diff. The claim's `additive` was not a member of the set; the dev corrected it and recorded the deviation.
- N1 below: the declaration line names two of the three new exports.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question 1 (empty referenced value: drop or gate) — answered, ruling 1: drop. The ruling's first reason ("the rule the picker already applies to an unset `dependsOn`") does not hold in the reader: an unset `dependsOn` parent GATES the picker (`dependenciesMissing`, `LookupField.tsx`); it never issues the query with the entry left out. The ruling's second reason (a market-less account must still see books) stands by itself, so the ruling is taken as answered; the false precedent is part of M1 because the JSDoc repeats it.
- Open question 2 (`$record` also names the flow run record) — answered, ruling 2: keep.
- Open question 3 (declared ahead of its reader) — answered, ruling 3: land with `[PLANNED — not enforced]` and the dated liveness note. Both are in the tree.
- Open question 4 (three exports) — answered, ruling 4: keep all three.
- Deviations: claim `additive` to `narrowed` (correct, see ②); PR opened before the local gate round, ADR-0122 alias red fixed at fb1e72c2 / 5664ba5f (the lint job is green on this head); schema block placed beside `FieldSchema` to keep governed `skills/**` indexes still (no `skills/**` path in the diff — confirmed); `check:generated` red under contention, green alone (the CI generated-artifact gates are green on the head). None needs escalation.
- Out-of-scope carriers (ui picker reader, server refusal by name, lint path check, `readonlyWhen` split, skills/docs): the rulings comment says the seat files them after merge. Not filed yet; that is the seat's stated plan, not a gap in this PR.
- Security: no `hits` path under `skills/**`; no finding.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`** — the shape holds: hop depth (`a.b` parses, `a.b.c` refused at `value.$record`), path syntax (per-segment field-key grammar; empty, camelCase, double dot, trailing dot, non-string refused), operators (`in` / `notIn` / `contains` refused at `value`), `orEmpty` pairing, closed reference object with pointed guidance for `addDays` and `$field`. `lookupFilters` is a flat AND list with no combinator, so `$record` inside `$or` / `$and` has no spelling to break. `$record` with `orEmpty` and an empty referenced value drops the whole entry (ruling 1). One sentence of the contract does not hold:

M1 (must-fix) — the `dependsOn` sentences are false against the live reader and against the `dependsOn` describe in the same schema. The `lookupFilters` describe says "those fields are implied — list one in `dependsOn` only to gate the picker until it is set"; the `LookupFilterRecordReferenceSchema` JSDoc says "listing one there adds only its gating" and calls leaving an empty entry out "the rule `dependsOn` already applies to an unset parent"; the changeset repeats the first. In the tree at this head a `dependsOn` entry does two things: it gates, and it adds an equality scope to the candidate query — `dependentFilter` in `ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx` writes `f[param] = value`, with `param` defaulting to the field name; the unchanged `dependsOn` describe says so ("it scopes the candidate query (string = same local/remote key…)"); and `packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.ts` binds a bare `dependsOn` name to BOTH the owner and the referenced object. On the card's own scenario, an author who follows the new describe and lists `date` (or `account`) in the Price Book lookup's `dependsOn` gets `date = 2027-01-05` added to the `crm_price_book` query, a column the book does not have, and a lint finding. The card body itself names this equality scoping as the reason `dependsOn` could not serve. No gate-only spelling exists today (`{ field, param }` scopes too). This is one of the five rules the ui follow-up is to be written against, and it contradicts the key it leans on. Fix in words or in shape: either state that `dependsOn` also scopes by equality, so a referenced field must NOT be listed there unless that scope is wanted (and drop the "already applies" precedent — an unset `dependsOn` parent gates, it does not drop), or declare a gate-only spelling and describe it on `dependsOn` too. The changeset sentence moves with it.

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.lookup-filter-record-reference-shape-refused.ts`** — `surface`, `replacement` and `reason` describe what the refinement refuses, and "never worked" is true on the reader and the drivers. One criterion fails:

S1 (should-fix) — `acceptanceCriteria` step (2), "opening that lookup's picker in the console lists candidates instead of an error", cannot hold in the release that ships this entry. The picker does not resolve `{ $record }` yet (the describes, the liveness note and the changeset's own warning all say an entry using `{ $record }` fails with `INVALID_FILTER` until the picker change ships), so an upgrader who rewrites to the declared shape still sees the error and reads the migration as failed. The `reason` has the same slant ("instead of being stored and failing on the first pick" — the declared shape also fails on the first pick this release). State that step (2) holds once the picker change ships, or make the criterion `objectstack validate` clean alone and name the picker caveat.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):
- N1 (nit) — the `Clause-②:` line (PR body and changeset) names `LookupFilterRecordReferenceSchema` and `LookupFilterRecordReference`; the third export, `LookupFilterRecordReferenceParsed`, is in api-surface and export-origins but not on the line.
- N2 (nit) — the semantic entry's `surface` and the changeset say "a lookup or master_detail field"; the refinement runs on `lookupFilters` of any field type, and a `user` field renders the same picker (`validate-object-field-refs.ts`).
- N3 (nit) — `{ field, operator: 'in', value: [{ $record: 'x' }] }` still parses: the shape test looks at the value object only, not at list members. Refused at query time as before; worth one sentence or one check in the lint follow-up.
- N4 (nit) — `field.test.ts` pins the door refusal for the six explicit-operator forms, `$eq` included, but the picker sends `eq` as the shorthand `{ field: { $record } }`, which passes the door and is refused by the driver. The card's market entry is that case and is unpinned here; the PR body says so and the server follow-up carries it.
- N5 (nit) — the describe does not say what a picker with no single edited record does (bulk-action selection bar, filter panel; `bulk-action.zod.ts` routes `lookupFilters` there). The empty-value rule covers it by extension; state it in the picker follow-up.

**Implementing files** — `field.test.ts`: 12 cases agree with the refinement sentence by sentence; the 2027-01-05 fixture is a test-local evaluator of the described lowering and does not exercise a reader (stated in its comment). The ledgers agree with the tree as judged in ①. No finding beyond N4.
